result.note: Tests India's data-centre incentives and Global AI Commons proposal, plus the investment projection and the Economic Survey's stance, from the February 2026 India AI Impact Summit.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's artificial intelligence policy as outlined around the India AI Impact Summit in February 2026:
items: India is pushing a "Global AI Commons", a shared repository of AI use-cases.
Data centres are being designated as "Strategic National Infrastructure".
Companies setting up data centres are offered tax holidays until 2047.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are stated in the story. The Global AI Commons aims to shape global AI norms around affordability rather than raw model power, and the data-centre incentives support a full-stack domestic AI cycle.
questions.source: By designating data centres as “Strategic National Infrastructure” and offering tax holidays until 2047, New Delhi is building an AI ecosystem with a focus on frugal, sector-specific applications rather than resource-heavy chatbots.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's AI strategy as of February 2026:
items: At the India AI Impact Summit, the IT Minister projected USD 200 billion in AI and data infrastructure investment over the next two years.
The Economic Survey 2025-26 backs a race to build frontier AI models for global prestige.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong: the Economic Survey 2025-26 explicitly rejects the prestige race of frontier models and favours frugal, sector-specific applications. Of the projected USD 200 billion, USD 70 billion was already committed.
questions.source: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw projected USD 200 billion in AI and data infrastructure investment over the next two years (USD 70B already committed) on Tuesday at the India AI Impact Summit.
